scenes.title: Thirty-Five Minutes
scenes.summary: M2 panics over the double-booked room while M1 unlocks the third-floor staircase.
scenes.intro: Rain taps against the lobby windows of the {SHOW} in {CITY}. With a second Room 7 guest arriving in thirty-five minutes, {M2}, {F1}, and {M1} hurry toward the stairs. Listen first.
story: M2
Thirty-five minutes! He will write a terrible one-star review!
F1
Take a deep breath, {M2}. Nobody has written anything yet.
M1
Here is the small silver key for the third-floor attic door.
M2
Does the attic even have a proper bed?
M1
Yes, a good wooden bed, a clean desk, and the best view in the house.
F1
Then why do we never rent it to guests?
M1
Because the stairs are narrow and {M2} keeps old lamp boxes there.
M2
Only three small boxes! Maybe four!
F1
We can move four boxes in five minutes. Let us go look right now!
M1
Up the stairs, turn left at the landing, last door at the top.
M2
I will bring clean white sheets from the linen cupboard!
F1
Come on—race you to the third floor!
scenes.outro: Thirty-five minutes on the clock and four boxes in the way—let's climb up to the third-floor attic next time.

scenes.title: The Sunny Attic
scenes.summary: Up in the quiet attic room, F1, M1, and F2 inspect the space and list what is missing.
scenes.intro: Up under the wooden eaves on the third floor, {M1} unlocks the attic study for {F1} while {F2} comes up carrying fresh towels. Let's listen to the whole scene first.
story: F1
Oh, look at this room! Big wooden beams and a window over the courtyard!
F2
Listen to the rain on the roof—it feels so cosy up here!
M1
Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.
F1
Okay: there is a bed, a table, and a chair, but no bedside lamp.
F2
And no mirror on the wall, and the floor feels bare without a rug.
M1
There is a brass reading lamp in my workshop downstairs.
F2
And I have two soft pillows and a woven blue rug in the store room!
F1
What about the small bathroom next door? Does the light work?
M1
New bulb last week, clean soap, plenty of hot water.
F2
Give us fifteen minutes and this attic will beat room seven!
F1
Grab those cardboard boxes, {M1}—down the stairs we go!
M1
Careful on the turn, do not bump the wall!
scenes.outro: With wooden beams and rain on the roof, the attic only needs a lamp, two pillows, and a rug. See you next time as they race the clock.

scenes.title: Left at the Landing
scenes.summary: F1, F2, and M2 finish making the bed, plug in the warm lamp, and hear the front gate bell.
scenes.intro: Ten minutes before eight, {F1}, {F2}, and {M2} put the finishing touches on the third-floor room. Every detail matters before the soaked traveller arrives. Listen first.
story: F2
Tuck that sheet corner tight, {F1}! Here go the two soft pillows.
F1
Done! And the blue rug fits right beside the bed.
M2
Where should I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?
F1
Right beside the desk, where the light is good.
F2
Plug in {M1}'s brass lamp... oh, look how warm that yellow light is!
M2
Honestly, I almost want to sleep up here myself tonight!
F1
Wait—what discount should we offer him for changing rooms?
M2
Half price for tonight, and free breakfast all week!
F2
Generous! Did you just hear the courtyard gate bell downstairs?
F1
Eight o'clock on the dot! Our guest is here!
M2
My heart is pounding! {F1}, you explain it—you sound calm and honest!
F1
Leave it to me. Let us go down and welcome him.
scenes.outro: The warm brass lamp is glowing just as the eight o'clock guest rings the downstairs bell. Next time, {M3} steps out of the rain.

scenes.title: In from the Rain
scenes.summary: Quiet architect M3 arrives soaked from the rain, and F1 and F2 warm him up before explaining the room change.
scenes.intro: Down in the lobby, quiet thirty-something traveller {M3} steps inside shaking out a wet umbrella. {F1} greets him at the desk while {F2} brings a warm towel. Listen first.
story: F1
Good evening! Come inside out of the rain, sir.
M3
Good evening. Sorry for dripping water on your clean floor.
F1
Do not worry at all! You must be {M3}.
M3
Yes, {M3}. I booked room seven by phone yesterday.
F2
Here is a dry towel for your coat and a cup of hot soup, sir.
M3
Hot soup? After that cold train platform, that sounds wonderful.
F1
Sir, before we go upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.
M3
Oh? Is there a problem with my booking?
F1
We accidentally wrote two bookings on room seven tonight.
M3
Ah... in this rain? Every hotel near the station looked full.
F1
Please do not worry! We prepared our quiet third-floor attic study just for you.
M3
An attic study? May I see it first?
scenes.outro: Honesty, a dry towel, and a cup of hot soup kept the conversation calm. Next time, {M3} climbs the stairs to judge the attic room for himself.

scenes.title: Half Price and Quiet Beams
scenes.summary: Shown the cozy attic room at half price, M3 admires the timber ceiling and happily takes the key.
scenes.intro: {M1} carries {M3}'s small travel bag up to the third floor while {F1} opens the door to the newly prepared attic room. Everyone holds their breath for {M3}'s verdict. Listen first.
story: F1
Here we are, sir. Watch your head on this low wooden beam.
M3
Oh... look at the proportions of this timber roof!
M1
Solid oak, eighty years old. Not a single leak.
F1
Because of our mistake, tonight is half price, with breakfast included.
M3
Listen for a second... you cannot hear a single car from the street.
F1
Only the courtyard tree and the rain.
M3
To tell you the truth, I hate noisy ground-floor rooms. I love this space!
M1
Really? You do not mind the extra stairs?
M3
Not at all! And this wide desk under the window is ideal for my work.
F1
What a relief! Here is your silver key, {M3}.
M3
Thank you both for being honest instead of sending me back into the rain.
M1
Sleep well, sir. Breakfast starts at seven thirty downstairs.
scenes.outro: Far from writing an angry review, {M3} fell in love with the quiet eighty-year-old oak beams! Let's head back downstairs next time.

scenes.title: A Five-Star Sigh of Relief
scenes.summary: Downstairs M2 celebrates the solved double-booking until F1 spots a small leather notebook left on the counter.
scenes.intro: Back at the ground-floor desk, {M2} is pacing nervously until {F1} comes down smiling to join him and {F2}. Then {F1} notices something lying beside the brass bell. Listen first.
story: M2
Well? Did he shout? Did he ask for his money back?
F1
Neither! He loved the quiet roof beams and thanked us.
M2
{F1}, you have a gift for hospitality! My blood pressure is saved!
F2
He even finished every drop of vegetable soup before going up.
F1
Wait—whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?
F2
{M3} set it down when he took the dry towel from me!
M2
Do not snoop, of course... wait, it fell open to the middle page!
F1
Why are there neat pencil drawings of three guesthouses on our street?
F2
Look at the words beside ours: 'Courtyard width, street noise, quiet score: nine out of ten!'
M2
Nine out of ten?! Nobody measures lobbies unless...
F2
Unless he writes for the annual {CITY} Travel Guide!
F1
Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs—wait, what is that loud clanking sound?
scenes.outro: Neat pencil sketches and a 'nine out of ten' rating have convinced them {M3} is a secret travel-guide inspector—just as a strange metallic clanking echoes through the house! See you next time.

scenes.title: Returning the Notebook
scenes.summary: F1 returns M3's leather notebook and hears the radiator pipe clank and go lukewarm.
scenes.intro: {F1} climbs up to the attic door to return {M3}'s forgotten leather notebook, trying hard to act normal despite thinking he is a secret hotel inspector. Listen first.
story: F1
Excuse me, {M3}? Sorry to disturb you.
M3
Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was just looking for it.
F1
You left it by the soup cup on the front counter.
M3
All my street notes from this week are in here. You saved me.
F1
We are glad you find our courtyard peaceful for your... work.
M3
Very peaceful! Though did you hear a funny metallic knock just now?
F1
Yes! It sounded like it came from the heating pipe in the corner.
M3
Feel the radiator—the top is warm, while the bottom is turning cool.
F1
Oh! Sometimes old pipes have a little air bubble at night.
M3
I have a warm blanket, so I am quite comfortable tonight.
F1
Thank you for being so patient! {M1} will check the basement right away.
M3
Good night, {F1}. See you at breakfast.
scenes.outro: {M3} got his notebook back without suspecting a thing, yet that cooling radiator is a warning sign. One final scene in Episode 3—down to the cellar! See you next time.

scenes.title: Ice-Cold Pipes
scenes.summary: Coming up from the cellar, M1 delivers bad news: the hot-water boiler valve just cracked for the night.
scenes.intro: Down at the front desk, {F1} and {M2} wait anxiously by the basement door until {M1} climbs up wiping his hands on a cloth and shaking his head. Listen first.
story: M2
Tell me it was just a tiny air bubble, {M1}! Please!
M1
Bad news. The brass pressure valve on the old boiler just gave up.
F1
Does that mean no radiators tonight, or no hot water too?
M1
The rooms will stay warm until morning, {F1}, because the brick walls hold heat.
M2
Thank heavens! And the morning showers?
M1
At seven tomorrow morning, the shower water will be ice-cold.
M2
Ice-cold showers?! With the {CITY} Travel Guide inspector on the third floor?!
F1
Do you have a spare brass valve in your toolbox?
M1
Used my last one in winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge sells this size.
F1
What time does that hardware shop open?
M1
Seven sharp—half an hour before breakfast.
F1
Set your alarm, {M1}. Tomorrow morning we beat the cold showers!
scenes.outro: A suspected travel-guide inspector upstairs, a broken brass valve in the basement, and a 7:00 AM race across the bridge tomorrow morning! Episode 3 is complete—see you in Episode 4.
